messages:
Maria S (AE): Heads-up — POC with FinServ customer failing in structured output + function-calls. They hit repeated parse errors and 429s during a 30-min test. Need eng help and a short workaround to unblock demos.
Alex S (Solutions): Summary of the issue from the customer: \"using function_call with json_mode=strict, responses sometimes arrive truncated or with extra commas, leading to 'Invalid JSON' on their side; also seeing intermittent rate-limit responses 429 with header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\"\nJordan (Runtime Eng): Can you paste the raw request/response and any x-request-id headers? Also which model/variant and whether streaming was enabled.
Maria S (AE): Pasting sanitized logs below — customer redacted some PII but kept headers. They use model: redwood-large-v2, streaming: false, json_mode: strict, function signature: process_transaction(payload: object) -> result.
```
REQUEST id=cr-abc123
POST /v1/generate
body: {"model":"redwood-large-v2","json_mode":"strict","function_call":{...}}
HEADERS: x-customer-id: cust-42, x-request-id: cr-abc123

RESPONSE 200
body: "{\n  \"result\": {\n    \"status\": \"ok\",\n    \"balance\": 12345,\n  }"  <-- trailing comma then truncated

Then later:
RESPONSE 429
HEADERS: x-request-id: cr-abc124, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 167
```
Devin (Oncall): Two things look likely: 1) A strict JSON serializer + post-hoc truncation is producing invalid JSON (trailing comma + abrupt EOF). 2) 429s indicate they exceeded the per-key burst QPS (we throttle to protect KV cache). Are they sending parallel calls with long max_tokens? Any client-side retry/backoff?
Maria S (AE): They ran a stress harness with ~40 concurrent sessions during demo. Retries were naive (no jitter). They also asked about pricing for Dedicated to avoid this.
Jordan (Runtime Eng): Workarounds to try now (quick):
- Switch json_mode from \"strict\" to \"lax\"/\"allow_partial_json\" (accepts partial objects and returns a checksum field)
- Reduce max_response_tokens / cap max_tokens to avoid chunking into an incomplete last token
- Add a response header: `X-Max-Response-Bytes: 24576` to force early truncation boundary
- For function-calls, prefer streaming=true + assemble chunks client-side with a robust JSON rejoin helper (we can share our helper snippet)
- Add exponential backoff and limit concurrency to <= 10 per API key while we investigate

Devin (Oncall): Also can you have them include the exact x-request-id from the 429 and the timestamp window? I'll correlate with ingress logs. If they can reproduce, tag the session and we'll pull the kernel logs.
Alex S (Solutions): Security ask: customer has a questionnaire re: Private deployment and KMS. They'll push for Private for non-prod first. Maria — can you copy which security controls they asked about so we can scope a Dedicated vs Private cost?
Maria S (AE): They're explicitly asking: encryption at rest, HSM/KMS integration, SOC2 controls, and network isolation (VPC). Also need per-tenant audit logs. I'll send back the spreadsheet. For now they want a temporary change to avoid failures during exec demo tomorrow.
Jordan (Runtime Eng): Immediate patch I'm willing to apply on our side: enable an internal tolerant JSON serializer for that customer's key for the next 24h (will allow trailing commas and close on EOF). It will be logged and reversible. But we need approvals from Security.
Security Bot: @engineering — automated policy check flagged \"tolerant-json-serializer\" as a configuration that increases parsing risk. Please request approval from Security and provide mitigation steps (audit logs, short TTL, read-only demo key).
Devin (Oncall): If Security approves, I can flip the flag and also add a temporary QPS bump for their test key (limit 25 -> 50) for 2 hours. We'll monitor for errors.
Alex S (Solutions): For pricing: Dedicated capacity estimate for this workload (30 concurrent, 1k tokens/session) — ballpark monthly commit egress + GPU reservation. I can draft a numbers email once we have measured per-token cost with/without caching.
Maria S (AE): Action items: 1) Jordan/devin — please try tolerant serializer + temp QPS bump if Security ok and tell me exact request-id header pattern we'll need. 2) Alex — draft a provisional Dedicated/Private cost summary for tomorrow demo. 3) I'll ask customer to switch to concurrency <=10 and add exponential jitter now.
Jordan (Runtime Eng): Will prepare a short helper script (node/python) that does chunk assembly + checksum verification for streaming mode and paste it here. If tolerant serializer is approved we'll still recommend long-term fix: client-side assembly or switching to structured function response with base64 payload to avoid comma problems.
Maria S (AE): Thanks. I'll coordinate approval with customer and security. I'll update thread with the x-request-id once they repro. :thumbsup:
Devin (Oncall): Logged: incident-scan id is inc-2026-03-21-42 — I'll attach kernel traces if we get repro.
Alex S (Solutions): If you want, cc me on the questionnaire responses. I can prefill the KMS/HSM answers.
Maria S (AE): Will do. Closing for now — will reopen thread when I have x-request-id.
